Aditya — quick ops note (internal):

This pattern is usually an organizer-affinity issue: when an invite is created by a non-canonical organizer or forwarded, GCal sometimes drops the conferencing block for cross-domain guests. Steps that reliably fix it:

1) Create the event with a Redwood service account (redwood-demo@redwood.ai) as the organizer and include the Zoom link in both the conferencing block and the body.
2) Set the Zoom meeting to require the host only for start/recording and allow participants to join before host (so NovuSec doesn't get stuck if we need to swap hosts).
3) If the customer's domain enforces calendar security settings, send them a direct .ics and ask an internal NovuSec organizer to accept — that binds their calendar.

If you want, I can spin up the Zoom meeting now and hand the moderator role to you once people join. I can also regenerate the .ics with UID tied to the Zoom meeting (that helps with propagation).

One more: include a one-line fallback in the invite body: "If you do not see a join button, use: https://zoom.us/j/9876543210?pwd=demo123" — that reduces help-desk replies.

Ben
